beats.say: Your pipeline works on your laptop. Good start.
Now it must run every night, retry on its own, and alert you when it is stuck.
beats.label: Now it must

beats.say: Two ideas: who conducts the work, and how you ship changes safely.
beats.label: Station 2.3 · Deploying the pipelines
beats.head: Orchestrate. Then ship safely.

check.prompt: One SQL query must run every night. What is enough?
check.why: A scheduled query runs SQL on a schedule. Composer is too much for one query.

beats.say: Think of an orchestra. Someone has to conduct.
Cloud Composer is managed Airflow. Pick it for big jobs with many steps, retries and backfills.
beats.label: Big, many steps
beats.head: Cloud Composer

beats.say: Workflows is light and serverless. Pick it for a short chain of API calls.
beats.label: A short chain of API calls
beats.head: Workflows

beats.say: Cloud Scheduler is just an alarm clock. It fires one thing, on a schedule.
beats.label: One thing on a clock
beats.head: Cloud Scheduler

beats.say: And for a single SQL query each night, a scheduled query is enough.
beats.label: Only SQL
beats.head: A scheduled query

beats.say: The trap: Composer for one nightly query. That is far too much.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Composer for one nightly query is overkill.

beats.say: One more. Airflow only conducts. The heavy work runs in BigQuery, Dataflow or Dataproc.
beats.label: Remember
beats.head: Airflow conducts. It does not play.

check.prompt: A retried task added the same rows a second time. What was missing?
check.why: An idempotent task overwrites its partition, so a retry changes nothing.

beats.say: A good task can run twice, and give the same result.
The word for that is idempotent. Overwrite the day's partition. Do not append again.
beats.label: Idempotent
beats.head: Overwrite the partition, do not append

beats.say: And use the run's date from Airflow, not the clock. Then backfills load the right day.
beats.label: Dates
beats.head: Use the run date, not "now"

beats.say: Idea two: shipping changes safely.
The rule is simple. Everything lives in Git. Nobody edits production by hand.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: Everything in Git. No hand edits.

beats.say: Cloud Build tests and deploys. Artifact Registry stores the images. Terraform builds the infrastructure.
beats.label: The toolbox

beats.say: With Terraform, dev, test and prod are built the same way. So what works in test works in prod.
beats.label: Why Terraform
beats.head: Dev, test and prod: identical

beats.say: Recap.
Composer for big DAGs. Workflows for light chains. Scheduler for one thing on a clock.
beats.label: Station 2.3 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Make tasks safe to run twice. And keep everything as code.
beats.label: Station 2.3 · 2 of 2
